::: {#exm-biased-variance-mle}
#### A biased estimator of the variance

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be mutually independent,
each with expectation $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$,
and let $n \ge 2$.
Consider two estimators of $\sigma^2$:

- the [sample variance](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-variance)
  $S^2 \eqdef \frac{1}{n-1} \sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - \bar X)^2$;
- the divide-by-$n$ estimator
  $\hat\sigma^2 \eqdef \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - \bar X)^2$.

Both estimators are built from the sum of squared deviations
$\sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - \bar X)^2$,
so we first find its expectation.
Using $\E{X_i^2} = \Var{X_i} + \sqf{\E{X_i}} = \sigma^2 + \mu^2$
and $\E{\bar X^2} = \Var{\bar X} + \sqf{\E{\bar X}} = \sigma^2/n + \mu^2$
(by @exm-mse-sample-mean and @exm-bias-sample-mean):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - \bar X)^2}
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n \paren{X_i^2 - 2 X_i \bar X + \bar X^2}}
&& \text{(expand each square)}\\
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2 - \sum_{i=1}^n 2 X_i \bar X + \sum_{i=1}^n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(split the sum)}\\
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2 - 2\bar X \sum_{i=1}^n X_i + \sum_{i=1}^n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(factor $2\bar X$ out of the middle sum)}\\
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2 - 2\bar X \sum_{i=1}^n X_i + n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\bar X^2$)}\\
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2 - 2\bar X \cdot n \bar X + n \bar X^2}
&& \text{($\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^n X_i = n \bar X$)}\\
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2 - 2n \bar X^2 + n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(multiply $2\bar X \cdot n \bar X$)}\\
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2 - n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(collect the $\bar X^2$ terms)}\\
&= \E{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2} - \E{n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \E{X_i^2} - \E{n \bar X^2}
&& \text{(linearity of expectation)}\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \E{X_i^2} - n \E{\bar X^2}
&& \text{(factor the constant $n$ out of the expectation)}\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n (\sigma^2 + \mu^2) - n \E{\bar X^2}
&& \text{(substitute $\E{X_i^2}$)}\\
&= n(\sigma^2 + \mu^2) - n \E{\bar X^2}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\sigma^2 + \mu^2$)}\\
&= n(\sigma^2 + \mu^2) - n\paren{\frac{\sigma^2}{n} + \mu^2}
&& \text{(substitute $\E{\bar X^2}$)}\\
&= n\sigma^2 + n\mu^2 - n\paren{\frac{\sigma^2}{n} + \mu^2}
&& \text{(distribute $n$ over $\sigma^2 + \mu^2$)}\\
&= n\sigma^2 + n\mu^2 - \paren{n \cdot \frac{\sigma^2}{n} + n\mu^2}
&& \text{(distribute $n$ over $\frac{\sigma^2}{n} + \mu^2$)}\\
&= n\sigma^2 + n\mu^2 - \paren{\sigma^2 + n\mu^2}
&& \text{(cancel $n$ in $n \cdot \frac{\sigma^2}{n}$)}\\
&= n\sigma^2 + n\mu^2 - \sigma^2 - n\mu^2
&& \text{(distribute the minus sign)}\\
&= n\sigma^2 - \sigma^2
&& \text{(cancel $n\mu^2$)}\\
&= (n - 1)\sigma^2
&& \text{(factor out $\sigma^2$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $\E{S^2} = \frac{1}{n-1}(n-1)\sigma^2 = \sigma^2$,
and by @thm-bias-exprs,
$\bias{S^2} = 0$:
the sample variance is [unbiased](#def-unbiased).

For the divide-by-$n$ estimator,
$\E{\hat\sigma^2} = \frac{1}{n}(n-1)\sigma^2$, so:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bias{\hat\sigma^2}
&= \E{\hat\sigma^2} - \sigma^2
&& \text{(bias equals expectation minus truth)}\\
&= \frac{n-1}{n}\sigma^2 - \sigma^2
&& \text{(substitute $\E{\hat\sigma^2}$)}\\
&= \frac{n-1}{n}\sigma^2 - \frac{n}{n}\sigma^2
&& \text{(write $\sigma^2$ over the common denominator $n$)}\\
&= \frac{n - 1 - n}{n}\sigma^2
&& \text{(combine the fractions)}\\
&= \frac{-1}{n}\sigma^2
&& \text{($n - 1 - n = -1$)}\\
&= -\frac{\sigma^2}{n}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\end{aligned}
$$

This estimator is biased:
on average it underestimates $\sigma^2$,
by an amount that shrinks to zero as $n$ grows.
:::
